text:
lena: Hey — running into flaky 'Event loop is closed' errors on Windows CI when tests use AsyncClient from the python SDK. Started after httpx bump and sdk 0.9.3. Anyone seen this?

raj: Can you paste the stacktrace? Is it during teardown or at import time?

lena: It's during teardown. Stacktrace: 
```
RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
  File "/workspace/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/httpx/_client.py", line 215, in aclose
    await self._transport.aclose()
  File "/workspace/sdk/redwood_async_client.py", line 128, in aclose
    await self._heartbeat_task
RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
```

sam: That looks like creating background tasks on module import or creating the client at module scope in pytest. On Windows CI the loop teardown order is different so the task tries to complete after loop closed.

olivia: I can reproduce locally if I do this: 
```py
# conftest.py
client = AsyncClient(api_key=... )  # module-scope

@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
async def sdk_client():
    yield client
    await client.aclose()
```

lena: yeah that's basically it. Creating AsyncClient before event loop exists -> background heartbeat scheduled on default loop, then pytest's loop policy closes it.

marc: Two separate but related issues i've seen: 1) We don't consistently await background tasks on close when the heartbeat cancels; 2) our AsyncClient typing is missing __aenter__/__aexit__ async context defs which encourages people to create clients at module scope instead of using async with. We should add typed async context manager support so linters suggest using `async with client:`

raj: opened a draft PR for the first fix (ensure tasks are awaited and don't re-schedule on close): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/pull/312 
Added a test that reproduces the Windows order by simulating loop close.

devex-bot: CI report: windows-latest py310 failed 1 job — flaky event-loop teardown observed. See logs.

sam: For immediate workarounds: 1) avoid module-scope AsyncClient, 2) use `async with AsyncClient(...) as client` in tests, or 3) explicitly call `asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(asyncio.WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy())` in CI if you're on older windows runner. Also `await asyncio.sleep(0)` after closing helps in some flakiness cases.

lena: There's also an auth/retry problem we noticed: when the async client retries (401->refresh->retry), the Authorization header is missing on the retry request, but the sync path preserves it. Anyone dug into retry middleware?

marc: That's a separate bug: our retry middleware shallow-copies the request object and mutates headers, but httpx async internals expect headers to be immutable lists — result is headers lost on re-send. I'll patch the middleware to re-create a new Request with preserved headers.

olivia: i'll add an integration test using httpx.MockTransport to assert the Authorization header exists on retries for async and sync paths.

raj: plan is to merge the event-loop + retry fixes, add tests, then cut 0.9.4 next week and cherry-pick to 0.9.x for the enterprise branch. PR numbers: #312 (loop), #318 (retry), #320 (typing/context manager + tests).

lena: awesome, thx. Any chance of a short snippet for the recommended test pattern so teams can patch their suites in the meantime?

sam: sure — suggested minimal pattern: 
```py
import pytest
from redwood import AsyncClient

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_use_context():
    async with AsyncClient(api_key=...) as c:
        r = await c.generate(...)
        assert r
```

and avoid creating clients at module scope. :thumbsup:

lena: great. i'll try the workaround and report back if CI still flakes. Thanks all! :100:
